sources.title: GitHub - RomainKH/Brimkern: The browser LLM engine that reads GGUF ...
sources.snippet: Every "AI in your browser" either wraps a remote API, or asks you to pre-compile the weights into its own artifact before it will touch them. Brimkern reads the format the Hub already hosts, single-file GGUF, and executes it with WGSL compute shaders we wrote by hand. That's the whole bet: the Hub holds tens of thousands of single-file GGUFs, and here every one of them is one paste away.

sources.title: Brimkern — Local WebGPU LLM engine in your browser
sources.snippet: .brik: a layer is one HTTP range Our container stores weights already quantized in the exact layout the kernels read, laid out so each layer is one contiguous range. A 4.7 GB model comes back from cache in 15.8 s — resumable, partial, genuinely offline afterwards.
